cues: The play has no scenes, so we follow its beats.
The plea: give me back my husband, Alfred, a blond, bespectacled lawyer.
The denial: the actress knows him only as the lawyer who drew up her contract; he never sent her a flower in his life.
The evidence: the wife learned at the florist that Alfred sends flowers twice a week, charged to his account; there is a letter, and a lock of hair.
Then the outburst: sobbing, the wife says the actress has cosmetics, bright lights and an author's lines to make her beautiful, while she has nothing.
